title: Why organizations use project management, and the challenges PRINCE2 tackles
blurb: Explain why organizations invest in project management and match common project challenges to the parts of PRINCE2 that tackle them.
question: A previous project kept spending money for a year after its expected benefits had disappeared. Which PRINCE2 principle is designed to stop this happening again?

teach.body: Organizations change through projects, and projects are riskier than routine work. Project management exists so that change is introduced in a controlled way: the investment stays justified, the extra threats and opportunities are managed, people from different functions are coordinated, and the work is delivered to the agreed targets for time, cost, quality, scope, benefits, risk and sustainability.

teach.h: Common reasons organizations use project management
items: To introduce change in a controlled way rather than by trial and error.
To keep the investment justified from start to finish.
To manage the extra uncertainty that projects carry.
To coordinate people with different skills who do not normally work together.
To deliver against agreed performance targets, not just 'get it done'.

What goes wrong

teach.caption: Challenges are paraphrased from manual 1.4; the responses are the PRINCE2 principles, practices and people element.

teach.h: Change introduced in a controlled way

teach.body: Brightwater Leisure Trust's last pool refurbishment overran by five months: nobody was sure who could approve changes, extra work crept in, and the board heard about the overspend too late. For the new gym project, Priya Raman is appointed project manager. The board agrees a business case and reviews it at each stage end, roles are written down, the scope is defined as products, and tolerances tell Priya exactly when she must escalate.

teach.text: Do not mix up manage by stages and manage by exception. Stages give the board planning and decision points; exception gives tolerances and escalation. A board flooded with minor decisions, or surprised by a late overspend, is a manage by exception problem.

teach.body: A classic challenge is applying a method identically to every project, producing paperwork without value. PRINCE2 answers this with the tailor to suit the project principle: the method is adapted to the project's environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and risk. The principles themselves are not tailored away.

items: Project management introduces change in a controlled way, keeps the investment justified and manages the extra uncertainty of projects.
It coordinates cross-functional people and delivers against agreed performance targets.
Typical challenges: weak justification, unclear roles, late-spotted overruns, scope creep, repeated mistakes, poor engagement.
PRINCE2 meets each with its principles, practices and people element, tailored to the project.

summary: You can now explain the common reasons organizations use project management. You can also match typical project challenges to the PRINCE2 principle, practice or element designed to tackle them.

A.q: Which is a common reason organizations use project management?
options: To replace line management of daily operations
To introduce change in a controlled way
To remove the need for a business case
To pass all project risk to the suppliers
A.why: Projects are the means of introducing change and are riskier than business as usual, so organizations use project management to introduce change in a controlled way.

whyNot.0: Daily operations stay with line management as business as usual; project management runs temporary projects.
whyNot.2: PRINCE2 projects are always justified by an agreed business case; project management relies on it.
whyNot.3: Project management manages risk within the project; it does not simply pass all of it to suppliers.

A.q: A previous project kept spending for a year after its expected benefits had disappeared. Which PRINCE2 principle most directly addresses this challenge?
options: Learn from experience
Manage by exception
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Ensure continued business justification
A.why: Ensure continued business justification requires the justification to be revalidated throughout; if the project is no longer justified, it should be stopped.

whyNot.0: Learning from experience helps avoid repeat mistakes, but the principle that stops an unjustified project is continued business justification.
whyNot.1: Manage by exception sets tolerances for escalation; it does not itself test whether the project is still worth doing.
whyNot.2: Defining roles makes clear who decides, but it does not test whether the project is still worth doing.

A.q: On a recent project, team members were unsure who could approve changes or who they reported to. Which principle addresses this challenge?
options: Manage by stages
Define roles, responsibilities and relationships
Ensure continued business justification
Learn from experience
A.why: A PRINCE2 project has defined and agreed roles and responsibilities within a structure that engages business, user and supplier interests, and builds relationships between stakeholders.

whyNot.0: Manage by stages provides decision points, not clarity about who holds which role.
whyNot.2: Continued business justification tests whether the project is still worth doing, not who holds which role.
whyNot.3: Learning from experience applies lessons; it does not establish who is accountable for what.

B.q: Why do projects need more deliberate coordination than business as usual?
options: They are run by external suppliers who sit outside the organization's control
They follow fixed routines that the team cannot adjust
They bring together people with different skills for a limited time
They have no budget until the final stage is authorized
B.why: Projects are cross-functional: people with different skills work together temporarily on a change affecting others, so coordination must be deliberate.

whyNot.0: Projects may use internal or external suppliers; being supplier-run is not the reason PRINCE2 gives.
whyNot.1: Fixed routines describe business as usual, not projects.
whyNot.3: Projects are funded through the business case and stage authorizations from the start, not only at the final stage.

B.q: Which challenge is the focus on products principle mainly designed to address?
options: Work expanding beyond what was agreed
Senior managers asked to make every decision
The same mistakes recurring on each project
A method applied identically to every project
B.why: Focus on products defines what the project will deliver, so it does no more work than needed and scope creep is controlled.

whyNot.1: Overloaded senior managers are addressed by manage by exception (tolerances and escalation).
whyNot.2: Recurring mistakes are addressed by learn from experience.
whyNot.3: A one-size-fits-all approach is addressed by tailor to suit the project.

B.q:
Which two statements about why organizations use project management are correct?
1. It helps keep the investment in a change justified throughout.
2. It removes the uncertainty that projects carry.
3. It helps coordinate people from different functions.
4. It is needed most where work repeats unchanged.
options: 1 and 2
1 and 3
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: Project management keeps the investment justified (statement 1) and coordinates cross-functional teams (statement 3).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is false: project management manages uncertainty; it cannot remove it.
whyNot.2: Statements 2 and 4 are false: uncertainty is managed, not removed, and repeated unchanged work is business as usual.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is false: repeated unchanged work is business as usual, not a project.

C.q: A project board was flooded with minor decisions, yet a serious overspend reached it too late to act. Which principle addresses this, and through what mechanism?
options: Manage by stages, through more frequent board meetings
Manage by exception, through tolerances and escalation
Focus on products, through detailed product descriptions
Learn from experience, through entries in a lessons log
C.why: Manage by exception sets tolerances for delegated authority and escalates forecast breaches early, so the board is not swamped yet is alerted in time.

whyNot.0: Manage by stages gives decision points at stage ends; it does not set the limits that trigger escalation.
whyNot.2: Product descriptions define what is delivered; they do not control when decisions are escalated.
whyNot.3: A lessons log records lessons; it does not set the limits of delegated authority.

C.q: People affected by a new working pattern were not consulted and resisted it after go-live. Which part of PRINCE2 7 most directly addresses this challenge?
options: The quality practice, through quality reviews of the products
The progress practice, through highlight reports to the board
The plans practice, through product breakdown structures
The people element, through communication and change management
C.why: The people element covers those working on and affected by the project; communication and change management (organizational transition) help affected people engage with and adopt the change.

whyNot.0: Quality reviews check products against their specifications, not stakeholder engagement.
whyNot.1: Highlight reports keep the project board informed of stage progress; they do not engage affected people.
whyNot.2: Product breakdown structures identify products for planning, not how to engage stakeholders.

C.q: An organization's old method required the same full set of documents on every project, however small. Which PRINCE2 principle answers this challenge, and what stays fixed?
options: Tailor to suit the project; the principles still apply
Tailor to suit the project; the roles cannot be combined
Manage by stages; every project has the same stage count
Focus on products; the document set is cut to the minimum
C.why: PRINCE2 is tailored to the project's environment, size, complexity, importance, delivery method, team capability and risk; what cannot be tailored away are the principles.

whyNot.1: Roles can be combined when tailoring (for example the project manager also acting as team manager), within rules such as one executive.
whyNot.2: The number of stages varies with the project; manage by stages does not fix a count beyond the minimum of two.
whyNot.3: Focus on products is about defining and delivering products, not about cutting management documents.

reteach.title: Think of a house extension
reteach.question: A family hires builders for an extension. What tends to go wrong without a structured approach, and what would fix each problem?

blocks.body: Without structure, the family keeps adding 'just one more' feature (scope creep), nobody is sure whether the architect or the builder decides (unclear roles), and they discover the overspend only when the final bill lands (late control). They also forget why they wanted the extension: a home office that would save commuting costs. PRINCE2 fixes each one: defined products, defined roles, stages with tolerances, and a business case checked throughout.

blocks.text: Stages give the family decision points (carry on, change course or stop); tolerances tell the builder when to come back to them. Two different principles.

explain.body: Projects introduce change and are riskier than routine work. Project management controls that change, keeps it justified, manages its uncertainty, coordinates mixed teams and delivers against agreed targets.

test.q: Which statement best explains why organizations use project management?
options: Routine operations need a separate method to run each day
Change brings uncertainty and must be introduced under control
Suppliers will not work without a certified project manager
Every piece of work must be divided into at least two stages
test.why: Projects introduce change and carry more uncertainty than business as usual, so organizations use project management to introduce that change in a controlled way.

whyNot.0: Routine operations are business as usual and are run by line management, not project management.
whyNot.2: Supplier requirements for certification are not a reason PRINCE2 gives for project management.
whyNot.3: The two-stage minimum applies to PRINCE2 projects, not to every piece of work.

explain.body: Projects often start with enthusiasm and carry on after the value has gone. PRINCE2 requires a business case that is checked and kept valid throughout; if the project is no longer justified, it should be stopped.

test.q: Which management product sets out the justification that PRINCE2 keeps checking throughout the project?
options: Risk register
Highlight report
Business case
Work package
test.why: The business case documents the justification for the project; it is developed, checked, maintained and confirmed through the lifecycle.

whyNot.0: The risk register records specific risks, not the overall justification.
whyNot.1: A highlight report updates the board on stage progress; it does not hold the justification.
whyNot.3: A work package is a set of work handed to a team; it does not justify the project.

explain.body: Overruns spotted late are a classic failure. Manage by stages gives the board decision points at the end of each stage; manage by exception sets tolerances so forecast breaches are escalated early.

test.q: Which principle gives the project board review and decision points at intervals through the project?
options: Manage by exception
Focus on products
Tailor to suit the project
Manage by stages
test.why: Manage by stages plans, monitors and controls the project stage by stage, giving the board review and decision points.

whyNot.0: Manage by exception sets tolerances and escalation, not the regular decision points.
whyNot.1: Focus on products defines and delivers products; it does not create decision points.
whyNot.2: Tailoring adapts the method to the project; it does not itself provide decision points.

explain.body: When nobody knows who decides, work stalls or the wrong person decides. PRINCE2 defines roles, responsibilities and relationships, and its organizing practice sets up the structure of accountability.

test.q: Through which practice does PRINCE2 tackle unclear accountability on a project?
options: Organizing
Plans
Progress
Quality
test.why: The organizing practice defines and establishes the project's structure of accountability and responsibilities.

whyNot.1: The plans practice defines what will be delivered and how, when and at what cost; the structure of accountability comes from organizing.
whyNot.2: The progress practice monitors and controls performance against plans.
whyNot.3: The quality practice ensures products are fit for purpose.
